verified.entry_point: The library's public factory: simpleGit(baseDir, options), then clone / mirror / fetch / pull / push / addRemote / raw, and the instance option key unsafe.allowUnsafeProtocolOverride. Every security case drives one of these; every functional case reads its result (returned value, the repository's files, or a recorded marker).
sites: simple-git/src/lib/plugins/block-unsafe-pack-plugin.ts (new): refuses upload/receive pack-program options on every spawn, and clone's -u shorthand

simple-git/src/lib/plugins/block-unsafe-operations-plugin.ts (new): refuses a protocol-permission override supplied as -c, --config, the attached spelling, or the instance configuration, unless the caller opts in
simple-git/src/lib/plugins/block-unsafe-remotes-plugin.ts (new): refuses storing a transport-helper remote address unless the caller opts in
simple-git/src/lib/git-factory.ts:59-61: registers the three guards on the shared spawn.args path
simple-git/src/lib/types/index.ts:110: adds the unsafe.allowUnsafeProtocolOverride opt-in to the instance options
routes: T1: clone with a pack-program option (object expansion, argument list) and the mirror alias
T2: pull with a pack-program option, push with a receive-program option, clone with the short form, raw clone with an explicit option
T3: clone or raw with a protocol-permission switch beside a helper address
T4: the same permission change through --config (one token and two tokens), the general protocol switch, and the instance configuration prefix
T5: a helper remote address stored by remote add, then used by a later fetch

Coupled functional: ordinary clone/fetch/pull/push/remote/raw, ordinary -c and --config configuration, commit messages and grep terms that contain helper-like text, the existing fetch refusal message, and the unsafe.allowUnsafeProtocolOverride opt-in for helper transports
verified.project_tests_run: The project's own unit suite (49 suites, 521 tests) passes at the pinned commit and with the reference fix; it is run in the environment image at build time. The hidden functional group adds 14 cases for the affected area.

patch_checks.why: fresh agent (deepseek-flash[1m]), full view (instruction, tree, tests, reference, trap list)

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: the library refuses by throwing; the security cases accept any thrown client error and judge the side effect, so a crash and a clean refusal are the same client-visible outcome here
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: there is no authorisation or resource model; the protected object is the argument list handed to the child process, so there is no neighbouring resource a fix could check instead
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: every route executes a command; there is no read/write or verb split in this library
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: the guards inspect the final argv at spawn, after the library's own option expansion; there is no offset, clamp or unit conversion on the caller value
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: no authority, role or secret lookup is involved; nothing can fail open on a missing secret

traps.shape: a clone (or its mirror alias) passes a caller-supplied option that names the program git runs for the transport; the pinned clone task passes every argument through unchanged
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the reported route; any acceptable fix covers it
traps.realistic_because: published advisory route (GHSA-28xr-mwxg-3qc8, CVE-2022-24066) at the pinned commit

traps.shape: the same program-selection token on the operations the published fix never touched: pull's pack option, push's receive-program option, clone's short spelling, and an explicit raw command
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the published fix extended the existing fetch check to clone only, so the option class reads as handled; the short clone spelling and raw look like separate escape hatches
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code at the pinned commit

traps.shape: a caller-supplied protocol-permission change beside a helper address; the pinned library passes both straight to git, which runs the helper
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the reported route; any acceptable fix covers it
traps.realistic_because: published advisory route (GHSA-9p95-fxvg-qgq2, CVE-2022-25912) at the pinned commit

traps.shape: the same permission change in the forms the published guard does not parse: the config alias in one or two tokens, the general protocol switch, and the instance configuration that the factory prefixes onto every spawn
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a guard keyed on the exact switch token looks complete; the alternative spellings and the configuration merged by the factory are not task arguments, so a task-level check never sees them
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code at the pinned commit; git accepts each spelling and the library accepts the instance configuration today

traps.shape: a helper remote address stored by the library for later use; the address never appears in the command that eventually runs it, so an argv check at that command cannot see it
traps.reason_to_dismiss: adding a remote only writes configuration and nothing runs at that moment; the danger appears at a later operation whose command line does not contain the address
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code at the pinned commit

advisories.summary: clone accepts a caller-supplied upload program; the fetch-side allowance had been fixed earlier (CVE-2022-24433), which is why the pinned tree already refuses it in fetch.
a caller-supplied protocol-permission configuration enables the ext transport helper; the advisory records it as an incomplete fix of CVE-2022-24066.
